title: Matcha Overnight Oats
changes_from_base: Uncooked: the oats and chia seeds soak in the fridge in milk whisked with matcha, maple syrup and vanilla, then are served with yoghurt and fresh fruit instead of being simmered.
summary: Earthy matcha and creamy yoghurt make these overnight oats a sustaining breakfast with pretty green colour and subtle caffeine lift.

ingredients.item: oat milk or whole milk, plus more to serve

steps.title: Prepare matcha
steps.text: Sift 1 tsp unsweetened matcha powder into a lidded tub (about 1000 ml).

steps.title: Add liquid
steps.text: Pour in 480 ml oat milk or whole milk, 35 ml maple syrup and ¼ tsp vanilla.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk thoroughly until smooth with no matcha lumps.

steps.title: Add oats
steps.text: Stir in 95 g rolled oats and 2 tbsp chia seeds.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate at least 3 h or overnight.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Before eating, stir well and loosen with a little more milk if you like, then divide between 4 bowls or glasses.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Crown each with 30 g Greek-style yoghurt and 37.5 g raspberries or other fresh fruit.

tips: Sift matcha before mixing to break up clumps and ensure a smooth blend.
Make these at least 3 hours ahead or the night before; they thicken as they sit, so loosen with extra milk if needed.
Matcha contains caffeine, roughly 15-20 mg per serving here, so bear that in mind for children or anyone avoiding it.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days; stir before eating and add more milk if the mixture is too thick. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
